title: Demand Curves for Stocks Do Slope Down
one_line: Stocks added to the S&P 500 (1976-1983) jumped ~3% on the announcement and the gain did not fully reverse, evidence that demand curves for stocks slope down (index-fund buying moves prices).

findings.statement: Announcement-day abnormal return ≈ +2.8% for additions after 1976 as index funds grew.
No full reversal over the following weeks.

why.pattern: Price pressure from mandated index buying.

reported_results.headline: Stocks added to the S&P 500 (1976-1983) jumped ~3% on the announcement and the gain did not fully reverse, evidence that demand curves for stocks slope down (index-fund buying moves prices).

tradable_edge: Stock-level; supports the price-pressure logic behind month-end/LETF index-futures specs.
data_fit: Single-stock study — not testable on our ES/NQ data.
